title: Ship evalkit as one static Go binary with the web UI embedded
context: The kit must be trivial to install and run for any agent or person: no runtime, no template files, no package manager.
decision: A single Go binary (cmd/evalkit) embeds the UI, the JSON Schema, the agent skill, the reference doc and the example suites. Releases build with CGO_ENABLED=0. Direct dependencies: gopkg.in/yaml.v3 and a JSON Schema validator.
consequences: go install or one downloaded file is the whole setup. UI edits need a rebuild unless serve --web <dir> is used.

title: Use Preact + htm with an import map and no build step
context: The UI is a registry of components composed from a schema. Vanilla DOM code re-implements diffing and loses focus on re-render; React with JSX needs a compiler and npm.
decision: Vendor Preact 10, preact/hooks and htm as ES modules mapped with an import map. Components use the React API with htm tagged templates.
consequences: Agents write familiar React-style code that ports 1:1 to React. No type checking in templates. Pure logic stays framework-free so node --test runs it.

title: Make JSON Schema the single source of truth for suite validation
context: Suites must fail loudly with file:line, item id, key and expected vs got, and editors want a schema file. A hand-written validator plus a separate schema would drift.
decision: Embed internal/suite/suite.schema.json, validate with a Go JSON Schema library, map JSON pointers back to YAML positions, and add semantic checks (references, uniqueness, key conflicts, proposals) in Go.
consequences: One schema serves the CLI, the server and editors. Library wording is less tailored, so the formatter adds item ids and allowed values.

title: Keep a fixed page layout and make content generic
context: Every eval should look and behave the same: buttons, spacing, colors, keyboard. A free-form layout language lets suites drift apart.
decision: The kit owns the layout: sidebar, toolbar, header, shown artifacts, a controls card, text questions, collapsed context. Suites choose content and order only.
consequences: Consistency by construction. A layout the kit lacks needs a kit feature, not suite markup.

title: Use CSS tokens with dark mode, and vendor Prism, uPlot and marked
context: Reviews need syntax-highlighted code, real charts and markdown, in light and dark mode, without a build.
decision: All colors are CSS variables with a prefers-color-scheme dark set. Vendor Prism (core plus 11 languages), uPlot and marked (raw HTML escaped), themed from the same tokens.
consequences: About 220 KB of vendored JS served locally; every renderer follows light and dark mode.

title: Keep feedback separate from input; never end the session on send
context: Globbing one directory for inputs and outputs renders snapshots as items, and stopping the server on send locks the reviewer out mid-review.
decision: State, numbered snapshots and action results live in feedback/ beside the suite. The server keeps running; evalkit wait polls the feedback directory for snapshots newer than the last one it reported.
consequences: Agents restart the waiter after each send; a late waiter still sees every send since its last report.

title: Drive per-row questions with a row cursor and number chords
context: Findings, extracted fields, rubric criteria and transcript steps all need answers per row, keyboard only, while number keys belong to the primary question.
decision: Up/Down move a cursor over rows that per-row questions target; per-row keys apply to the cursor row. A question's key followed by a digit picks option N (or value N on a scale).
consequences: Up/Down do not scroll on items with rows. The help sheet spells out every chord.

title: Add when conditions instead of nested follow-up questions
context: Corrections apply only to wrong fields, reasons only to rejections. Label Studio's visibleWhen is the prior art.
decision: A question may declare when: {questionId: [values]}. It is shown, and its answer kept in the snapshot, only while that holds, per row for per-row questions.
consequences: Answers typed under a condition that later fails are dropped from the snapshot but kept in state.

title: Version the review state so a stale tab cannot overwrite it
context: State is saved whole; a second, older tab would silently replace newer answers and could send a snapshot without them.
decision: State carries an integer rev. Saves and sends post the rev they loaded; the server answers 409 when it changed, and the page reloads the newest state with a notice.
consequences: Saves are serialized in the page. Two tabs can be open safely; the older one reloads instead of winning.

title: Keep the CLI to init, serve and wait, with everything else discoverable
context: Anyone starting a project should get from nothing to agent feedback in three commands, without reading the repo.
decision: Every command defaults to ./suite.yaml; init writes a starter (or the every-kind example); docs, schema and skill print embedded files; skill --install teaches Claude Code the loop; help shows per-command examples.
consequences: The binary carries its own documentation; changes to docs or examples need a rebuild to reach installed users.

title: Model judge scores as proposals and measurements as read-only values
context: Automated judge loops (eval harnesses, hill-climbing rounds) grade dozens to hundreds of rows. The human spot-checks and corrects the judge; cost, latency and deterministic checks are facts nobody should edit.
decision: Judge verdicts and scores are proposed answers to ordinary questions (choice for labels, number with min/max for 0-10 or 0-1 scores). Measurements go in item values, declared by suite columns. Both may carry a baseline. No score kind was added.
consequences: Overrides come back as changed {from, to}, which is the judge's calibration data, with no new protocol. The table derives every column from the suite; only columns is new.

title: Feed judge rows through items_from JSONL
context: Harnesses already append one result per line to results.jsonl while they run; rewriting a whole suite per row is awkward and racy.
decision: A suite may declare items_from: JSONL paths or globs, one item per line, appended after items. A later line with the same id replaces the earlier one in place; a partial last line is skipped; a missing file is a warning. Problems name the JSONL file and line. /api/version hashes the files instead of validating them.
consequences: evalkit serve can start before the first row and the page fills in live. A loop regrades a row by appending it again. Large suites stay cheap to poll.

title: Give every suite a table view that shares filters with review
context: Review mode shows one item at a time, which does not scale to a judged round where most rows need no human.
decision: The toolbar switches between Review and Table; Enter opens the selected row and Esc returns. Column headers profile the rows in view (histogram, share bar, delta counts) and filter on click. Opening review from a filtered or sorted table pins those rows as the list J and K walk, so answering an item out of the filter does not reshuffle navigation. view: table sets the default; ?view= overrides it.
consequences: No per-view schema. The sidebar and J/K follow the table's filter. Flagged items (item flag) define progress when present.

title: Hold many runs of one eval in one suite
context: Hill-climbing rounds, model sweeps and weekly samples repeat the same cases; comparing them meant one suite per run or a baseline on every value.
decision: A suite lists runs:, each with its own items_from, dims and optional baseline: true; dimensions: name what varies. The loader gives run items the id run/id (.rN for a rep) and a pair key, so state, feedback and evalkit wait keep unique ids unchanged. Runs pair items by pair; each run is compared with the marked baseline, else the run before.
consequences: Harness output needs no change: a run's items_from sets run on every line. Inline baselines are ignored with runs. A suite without runs loads byte for byte as before. evalkit done stores run/id as run~id.

title: Compute run statistics in the page and chart them with Observable Plot
context: A reviewer's overrides should move every score and comparison at once, and the Runs view needs line, scatter, frontier and stacked-bar charts in light and dark.
decision: web/kit/core computes intervals (Wilson for a rate, a seeded case bootstrap for a mean or a rate with reps), paired changes and McNemar's exact test. Run charts use Observable Plot 0.6.19, vendored as one ES module (131 KB gzip) and drawn with the UI's CSS tokens; the table's micro charts stay plain SVG.
consequences: No server-side statistics and no build step. Colors flip with the theme without a redraw. scripts/vendor-plot.sh regenerates the bundle.

title: Lay out the Runs view as tiles, a runs table, then charts
context: The user wanted a dashboard of runs with no charts in popovers or modals and no charts inside table cells; a runs table placed between chart cards was hard to find.
decision: Runs is a third view before Table and Review. Top to bottom: tiles for the selected run, a Runs card with a numbers-only table of every run, the run-by-run and score-against-spend charts, then each case before and after. The table and review show one run at a time, named in the toolbar, with [ ] to step runs and Esc to climb back to Runs.
consequences: Picking a run and reading it stay together at the top. A suite with runs opens on the table unless view: runs. No score chip in the toolbar.

title: Let a compare artifact span the full page width
context: Reviewing a test-pruning run means reading a deleted test beside the test that keeps its proof. Two width: half code artifacts gave each about 470 px of the 980 px reading column and cut lines off; the user called it cramped and asked for a full-width split.
decision: A new built-in kind, compare, shows two or three code panes side by side. A renderer that sets wide = true leaves the reading column and spans the scroll area, keeping 40 px gutters, through a container query on the scroll area; panes stack below 900 px. Prose, controls and every other artifact keep the 980 px column.
consequences: Code comparisons get about half the page each, and a Wrap toggle folds long lines. Line length for prose is unchanged. Custom renderers can opt in to full width the same way.

title: Keep one full-width top bar in every view
context: In Review the toolbar sat over the main column beside the sidebar; in Table it spanned the window, so switching views moved the Review/Table toggle and the Send button and changed widths. The user found the jump jarring.
decision: The top bar spans the window in Review, Table and Runs with the same controls in the same places. The suite title, description and progress sit under the top bar's line in every view, and the sidebar starts below it. Switching views animates with the View Transitions API (the sidebar slides away and the content takes its space), instantly when the API is missing or reduced motion is set.
consequences: Nothing in the top bar moves between views. Previous/next and the counter also show in Table, stepping the selected row. Only the latest of several fast switches applies.

title: Vendor @pierre/diffs as one trimmed module for split diffs
context: The user wanted left/right split diffs in compare and diff artifacts using @pierre/diffs, themed, with an ultra-minimal dependency footprint. A plain bundle of the package is 1.79 MB (571 KB gzipped): it pulls every Shiki grammar and theme, the WebAssembly regex engine and an alternative highlighter.
decision: scripts/vendor-diffs.sh bundles only FileDiff and parsePatchFiles with esbuild into web/vendor/diffs.esm.js. build.mjs replaces the Shiki language and theme catalogs, the WebAssembly engine and @pierre/highlights with stubs; entry.js registers the Pierre light and dark themes and eight grammars. The page loads the module the first time a diff view opens. Licenses of every bundled package go to web/vendor/diffs.LICENSES.txt.
consequences: 914 KB (190 KB gzipped), loaded only on demand. Split views use the Pierre themes and follow the system light or dark setting; evalkit's own code renderers keep Prism. A language outside the eight grammars shows as plain text in a split view. Upgrading is one command with the new version.
